title: The three layers plus discovery
lede: Every 'it doesn't work' ticket is a mismatch between two layers: Identity (what the agent is), Grant (what it may reach), Guardrail (what screens its traffic). Discovery sits above: what agents exist that you didn't onboard yourself.

nodes.label: The agent
sub: wants models, MCP tools or A2A agents

nodes.label: Agentic Apps
sub: MCP servers, A2A agents, LLM providers
the doors a grant points at

nodes.label: Grant (policy)
sub: auto-created by app selection on a key
or authored: pacpolicys for federated ids

nodes.label: Per-key AI Guard
sub: rate limits enforced at the gateway

steps.title: The agent calls
steps.what: No identity, no call. The agent either presents an Agent Registry access key (Bearer, no sign-in, no token exchange) or a platform-issued JWT under Federated Identity.

steps.title: Identity resolves
steps.what: A key carries its scopes, models, caps and custodian on itself. A federated identity pins issuer, audience, subject and required claims — and still needs a key behind it: an NHI authenticates nobody by itself.

steps.title: The grant scopes the reach
steps.what: Selecting apps on a key IS the grant — saving auto-creates a policy. For federated identities the grant is an authored policy (pacpolicys) gated on token claims. Scoped to MCP tools, A2A agents or LLM providers/models.

steps.title: The guardrail screens the call
steps.what: Per-key AI Guard is a runtime protection step; rate limiting is enforced natively at the gateway. This is where prompt-injection and data-exfil controls sit.

steps.title: Discovery covers what you didn't onboard
steps.what: Self-Hosted Agents find shadow agents in your own infrastructure and attach enforcement. AI Platform Agents control what third-party platform agents do when they cross into your estate.
